data:
Status: planned (wave 3). There is no repository and no code yet, and graph is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
Graph algorithms that gonum/graph lacks, behind a MATLAB-style graph and digraph facade.
data.depends-on#Depends on: gonum/graph. The organization extends or wraps gonum and does not duplicate it; the maintainers’ stance on adding matching upstream is an open question in the plan.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Exact equality for integer-weight shortest paths, flow values, matching sizes and component partitions. Modularity within a tolerance for community detection, with the seed fixed; labels are not compared. Corpora: SNAP and the DIMACS implementation challenges.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use gonum/gonum graph/... BSD-3-Clause; imported directly (https://github.com/gonum/gonum). It has Dinic maximum flow, Brandes betweenness, PageRank, HITS, Louvain and Leiden; it has no matching, no push-relabel and no Sugiyama layout NetworkX BSD-3-Clause; the oracle for every graph algorithm, driven from Go with node-link JSON Boost.Graph BSL-1.0; permissive, usable as a reference igraph C core GPL-2.0: an oracle only GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.

data.scope-notes#Scope notes: Graph layout is not part of this organization: it belongs to go-graphdrawing (https://github.com/go-graphdrawing), which is empty today and depends on this one.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: facade graph and digraph with adjacency, incidence and Laplacian matrices, over gonum/graph matching Hopcroft-Karp (bipartite) and blossom (general) isomorphism VF2, and canonical labelling cuts and flows minimum-cut extraction; push-relabel if gonum’s Dinic is not enough centrality the remaining centralities reused, not rewritten shortest paths, spanning trees, strongly connected components, Brandes betweenness, PageRank, HITS, Louvain and Leiden, which gonum/graph already provides
data.where-the-plan-lives#Where the plan live: PLAN.md, STATUS.md and the bibliography in the go-scikit roadmap.
